343166.title: Difference-set graceful-labeling conjecture for regular connected graphs

literal.statement:
Let $D$ be a $(v,k,\mu)$ difference set in a group $G$, and define

$$
\lambda_i=\frac{\mu i}{\gcd(k-1,\mu)}
$$

$$
\frac{(k-1)i}{\gcd(k-1,\mu)}
$$

is $D$-graceful; consequently, there exists a $(v,\Gamma,\lambda_i)$ difference graph with vertex set $D$. The conjecture is motivated by the absence of counterexamples for regular connected graphs of order $|D|$; the source records no general proof, although it notes later special cases for Paley difference sets and circulant graphs.

343308.title: The generalized Hamming polynomial reconstruction formula for combinatroids

literal.statement:

$$
W^{(r)}(x,y,q):=\frac{1}{\langle r\rangle_q}\sum_{j=0}^r \left[\begin{array}{c}r\\ j\end{array}\right]_q(-1)^{r-j}q^{\binom{r-j}{2}}(x-y)^{n-k}y^kT_M\left(\frac{x}{y},\frac{x+(q^j-1)y}{x-y}\right).
$$

$$
T_M(x,y)=x^n(x-1)^{k-n}\sum_{r=0}^{n-k}\left(\prod_{j=0}^{r-1}\bigl((x-1)(y-1)-q^j\bigr)\right)W^{(r)}(1,1/x,q).
$$

This formula proposes that the Tutte polynomial of a combinatroid can be reconstructed from its generalized Hamming weight enumerators. The supplied text does not indicate whether the statement has been proved or disproved.

338620.title: The exponential field-size conjecture for random set systems

literal.statement:
Let $S_1,\ldots,S_k\subset[n]$ be random sets, formed by including each $j\in S_i$ independently with probability $1/2$. A matrix $A$ satisfies the associated zero-pattern conditions when

$$
A_{i,j}=0\quad\text{whenever }j\in S_i,
$$

and every $k\times k$ minor not forced to be singular by these zero constraints is nonsingular.

**Exponential field-size conjecture.** Assume that such a $k\times n$ matrix exists over a field $\mathbb{F}$. Then, with high probability over the random set system, there is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that

$$
|\mathbb{F}|\ge c\binom{n}{k}^{c}.
$$

The conjecture asserts that most set systems require exponential field size, so the probabilistic construction with field size roughly $\binom{n}{k}$ cannot be significantly improved. The source presents it as an open problem; only specialized examples requiring exponential field size are known.

$$

$$

$$
This predicts the threshold for the asymmetric Ramsey property of a random graph; the source notes that the conjecture is actually stated for $r=2$ and describes the threshold as sharp. Its resolution status is not established by the supplied material.

literal.statement:

$$
\mathcal A_i^{(k)}(n,s):=\Bigl\{A\in {[n]\choose k}:\bigl|A\cap[(s+1)i-1]\bigr|\ge i\Bigr\},
$$

and define

$$
\mathcal H^{(k)}(n,s):=\Bigl\{H\in {[n]\choose k}:H\cap[s]\ne\emptyset\Bigr\}\cup\bigl\{[s+1,s+k]\bigr\}-\Bigl\{H\in {[n]\choose k}:H\cap[s]=\{s\},\ H\cap[s+1,s+k]=\emptyset\Bigr\}.
$$

**Hilton–Milner-type conjecture.** If $\nu(\mathcal F)=s$ and $\tau(\mathcal F)>s$, then

$$
|\mathcal F|\le\max\Bigl\{\bigl\{|\mathcal A_i^{(k)}(n,s)|:i=2,\ldots,k\bigr\},|\mathcal H^{(k)}(n,s)|\Bigr\}.
$$
 This conjecture seeks the sharp bound for families with matching number exactly $s$ that are not covered by $s$ elements, generalizing the Hilton–Milner phenomenon; its resolution status is not specified in the source.

323005.title: Near-symmetry conjecture for generating functions of leafed-cycle cones of power-of-two length

literal.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}_{2^k}$ be the cone constrained by the Laplacian minor of a leafed $n$-cycle, where $n=2^k$ for some integer $k\geq 2$. Let $f(q)$ be the numerator in the proposed expression

$$
\sigma_{\mathcal{C}_{2^k}}(q,1,1,\ldots,1)=\dfrac{f(q)}{\left(1-q^{2^k}\right)\displaystyle\prod_{i=0}^{k-1}\left(1-q^{2^{k-(i+1)}}\right)^{2^i}}.
$$

**Near-symmetry conjecture.** The generating function has this form, and if $(a_0,\ldots,a_j)$ is the coefficient list of $f(q)$, then appending $0$ to the end of this list and subtracting its reverse produces the coefficient list of

$$
\sum_{i=0}^{n-2}\binom{n-2}{i}(-1)^i q^{ni}.
$$

This conjecture is based on experimental evidence for leafed cycles of length a power of two and describes the observed near-symmetry of the numerator despite the absence of a reflexive $n$-th slice in the non-prime case.

338745.title: The List Equitable Total Coloring Conjecture

literal.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, let $T(G)$ be its total graph, and let $\chi_l(T(G))$ denote the list chromatic number of $T(G)$. A graph is **equitably $k$-choosable** if every list assignment with lists of size $k$ admits a proper coloring in which each color is used on at most $\lceil |V(T(G))|/k\rceil$ vertices. **The List Equitable Total Coloring Conjecture.** For every graph $G$, the total graph $T(G)$ is equitably $k$-choosable for every

$$
k\geq\max\{\chi_l(T(G)),\Delta(G)+2\}.

331056.title: The 1-2-3 Conjecture on neighbour sum distinguishing edge colourings

literal.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with no isolated edges. For an edge colouring $c:E(G)\to\{1,2,\ldots,k\}$, define the weighted degree of a vertex $v$ by

$$
s_c(v):=\sum_{u\in N(v)}c(uv).
$$

The colouring is **neighbour sum distinguishing** if $s_c(u)\neq s_c(v)$ for every adjacent pair $u,v$.

**1-2-3 Conjecture.** Every graph $G$ containing no isolated edges admits a neighbour sum distinguishing $3$-edge colouring.

A neighbour sum distinguishing $5$-edge colouring is known for every graph without isolated edges, but whether three colours always suffice remains open. The conjecture is equivalent to seeking a locally irregular multigraph obtained by replacing each edge with a number of parallel edges from $1$ to $3$.
